verdict.rationale: Factory's docs say that "a designer shares a mockup, and the system implements it without handoffs." That line sits in the Agent Readiness overview, so it describes a state that depends on repository readiness rather than a documented mockup-to-code workflow. Adjacent first-party capabilities support the story: Design mode lets a user select an element and say what to change, with Droid acting on the feedback in place. Users can also assign Linear or Jira issues for Droid to implement and test, then review the diff and merge from the App. Missing for 10: documented mockup or image ingestion into an implementation flow, step-by-step docs for a non-engineer persona, an explanation of what readiness is required for handoff-free delivery, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a product-manager, I can go from a mockup or design to a working implementation without an engineering handoff

citations.quote: A designer shares a mockup, and the system implements it without handoffs.
Design mode selects an element and says what to change; inline code review comments on a diff line by line. Droid acts on the feedback in place.
Assign a Linear issue to Factory or mention `@Factory` in an issue comment to have Droid investigate, implement, and test the work.
Delegate a task, review the diff, and merge from the App or your terminal.
